title: Get a dog license
question: Does my dog need a city license, and how do I get one?
summary: Every dog 4 months or older kept in Charlottesville must be licensed within 30 days of turning 4 months or being acquired. Since 2018 the City sells only lifetime licenses, at $10 per dog. Mail the City's Dog License Application to the Treasurer's Office (P.O. Box 2854) or bring it to the Treasurer's counter in the City Hall lobby, with a current rabies vaccination certificate (or a rabies vaccination exemption certificate from the local health director) and payment. You get a receipt and a metal tag for the dog's collar. The license lasts while you live in the city and keep the rabies vaccination current. A lost tag costs $1 to replace. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs pay no tax. Keeping an unlicensed dog is a Class 4 misdemeanor.

legal_basis.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person other than a releasing agency that has registered as such annually with local animal control to own a dog four months old or older in the Commonwealth unless such dog is licensed, as required by the provisions of this article.
The governing body of each county or city shall impose by ordinance a license tax on the ownership of dogs within its jurisdiction.
The tax for each dog or cat shall not be more than $10 for each year or $50 for a lifetime license

No license tax shall be levied on any dog that is trained and serves as (i) a guide dog for a blind person, (ii) a hearing dog for a person who is deaf or hard of hearing, or (iii) a service dog for a mobility-impaired or otherwise disabled person.
The provision of emotional support, well-being, comfort, or companionship shall not constitute work or tasks for the purposes of this definition.
The owner or custodian of all dogs and cats four months of age and older shall have such animal currently vaccinated for rabies
such exemption shall be considered in place of a current certificate of vaccination
A dog or cat license shall consist of a license receipt and a metal tag.

No license tag shall be issued for any dog or cat unless there is presented, to the treasurer or other officer of the locality, or other agent charged by law with the duty of issuing license tags for dogs and cats, satisfactory evidence that such dog or cat has been inoculated or vaccinated against rabies

by making oral or written application to the treasurer of the locality where such person resides, accompanied by the amount of license tax and current certificate of vaccination as required by this article or satisfactory evidence that such certificate has been obtained

shall only have authority to license dogs and cats of resident owners or custodians who reside within the boundary limits of his county or city and may require information to this effect from any applicant
The treasurer may establish substations in convenient locations in the county or city and appoint agents for the collection of the license tax and issuance of such licenses.

The veterinarian shall forward within 45 days a copy of the rabies vaccination certificate or the relevant information contained in such certificate to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination occurs.

has failed to apply for a license within 90 days of the date of vaccination, the treasurer shall transmit an application to the owner and request the owner to submit a completed application and pay the appropriate fee

The license tax as prescribed in § 3.2-6528 is due not later than 30 days after a dog or cat has reached the age of four months, or not later than 30 days after an owner acquires a dog or cat four months of age or older, and each year thereafter.
Such a license shall be valid only as long as the animal's owner resides in the issuing locality and the animal's rabies vaccination is kept current.
Any kennel license tax prescribed pursuant to § 3.2-6528 shall be due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year.
"Kennel" means any establishment in which five or more canines, felines, or hybrids of either are kept for the purpose of breeding, hunting, training, renting, buying, boarding, selling, or showing.
Dog license tags shall be securely fastened to a substantial collar by the owner or custodian and worn by such dog.
Dog and cat license receipts shall be carefully preserved by the licensees and exhibited promptly on request for inspection by any animal control officer or other officer.
The fee for a duplicate tag for any dog or cat shall not exceed $1.
Any dog or cat not wearing a collar bearing a valid license tag shall prima facie be deemed to be unlicensed
For any dog or cat owner to fail to pay any license tax required by this chapter before February 1 for the year in which it is due.
For Class 4 misdemeanors, a fine of not more than $250.

Payment of the license tax subsequent to a summons to appear before a court for failure to pay the license tax within the time required shall not operate to relieve such owner from the penalties or court costs
shall require dogs running at large without the tag required by § 3.2-6531 or in violation of an ordinance passed pursuant to § 3.2-6538 to be confined therein
The local health director, in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, may grant an exemption to the requirement for rabies vaccination

Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination may be presented in lieu of a rabies vaccination certificate for the purposes of veterinary inspection by designated local authorities and for the purposes of licensing by the locality where the animal resides.

Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination shall be valid for one year, after which time the animal shall be vaccinated against rabies or the application for exemption shall be renewed.

It shall be unlawful and a Class 4 misdemeanor for any person to own or keep within the city any dog four (4) months old or older for which a current license has not been secured as provided by the laws of the state.
The dog license tax, payable at the office of the city treasurer, shall be as follows:
For any individual dog, a lifetime license tax of ten dollars ($10.00).
For a kennel of twenty (20) dogs, twenty dollars ($20.00) annually.
For a kennel of fifty (50) dogs, thirty-five dollars ($35.00) annually.
The lifetime license shall be valid only as long as the animal’s owner resides in the City of Charlottesville and the dog’s rabies vaccination is kept current.
A fee of one dollar ($1.00) will be charged for replacement of a dog license that is lost or stolen.
The license for a kennel shall run from January 1 to December 31, inclusive.

No license tax shall be levied on any dog that is trained and serves as a guide dog for a blind person or that is trained and serves as a hearing dog for a deaf or hearing impaired person or that is trained and serves as a service dog for a mobility-impaired person.

steps.step: Check whether your dog needs a city license
steps.who: The dog's owner or custodian who lives in the City of Charlottesville
steps.how: Every dog 4 months old or older that is kept in the city must be licensed. Releasing agencies (shelters, humane societies and rescues that release animals for adoption) are exempt only if they have registered as such annually with local animal control. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs are still licensed but pay no license tax (see s5). If you live outside the city limits, even with a Charlottesville mailing address, you license the dog with your own county or city treasurer instead.
steps.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old, or not later than 30 days after you acquire a dog 4 months old or older (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.quote: City of Charlottesville Code Section 3.2-65 requires that all dogs in the city that are 4 months old and older wear a current dog license.

steps.step: Have the dog vaccinated against rabies and keep the certificate
steps.who: Owner; a licensed veterinarian (or a licensed veterinary technician under a veterinarian's direct supervision)
steps.how: The veterinarian gives you a rabies vaccination certificate and, by law, also sends a copy (or its details) to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination happens, within 45 days. You need the current certificate, or a copy sent by your veterinarian, before the Treasurer can issue a license.
steps.deadline: The dog must be currently vaccinated from 4 months of age (Va. Code § 3.2-6521(A))
steps.quote: The supervising veterinarian on the premises shall provide the owner or custodian of the dog or the cat with a rabies vaccination certificate or herd rabies vaccination certificate and shall keep a copy in his own files.

steps.step: Only if the dog cannot safely be vaccinated: get a medical exemption certificate
steps.who: Your veterinarian applies; the local health director (Virginia Department of Health), in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, decides
steps.how: The veterinarian consults the local health director and submits the Department of Health exemption request form with the dog's medical records. If approved, the health department issues a rabies vaccination exemption certificate to the veterinarian, the owner and the local animal control office. You present that certificate to the Treasurer instead of a vaccination certificate. The exemption counts in place of a vaccination certificate only for licensing and inspection: if the dog is exposed to a confirmed or suspected rabid animal it is treated as unvaccinated. A locality may require an exempted dog to be confined on the owner's property, leashed or otherwise restrained, or to carry a unique identification (12VAC5-105-30(C)); whether Charlottesville does was not checked.
steps.deadline: The exemption certificate is valid for one year, after which the dog must be vaccinated or the exemption renewed (12VAC5-105-30(B))
steps.quote: Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination may be presented in lieu of a rabies vaccination certificate for the purposes of veterinary inspection by designated local authorities and for the purposes of licensing by the locality where the animal resides.

steps.step: Fill in the City's Dog License Application
steps.how: Download the application (PDF, fillable). It asks for the owner's name, address and phone number, and for each dog its name and rabies expiration date, at $10 per dog. Attach a copy of the current rabies certificate, or ask your veterinarian to send the Treasurer's Office a copy.
steps.quote: Please complete this form and mail or return it to the Treasurer’s Office at the address above with a copy of a current rabies vaccination certificate and payment.

steps.step: Submit the application, the rabies certificate and the license tax to the City Treasurer
steps.how: Either mail the application, a copy of the certificate and a check or money order to City of Charlottesville, Treasurer's Office, P.O. Box 2854, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (do not mail cash), or bring them to the Treasurer's customer service counter in the lobby of City Hall, 605 East Main Street, Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, except legal holidays. The counter takes cash, checks, debit cards and money orders. The City's phone and online payment lists do not include dog licenses. You may bring the original certificate to be checked. For a trained guide, hearing or service dog, tell the Treasurer: state law says no license tax is charged for it.
steps.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old or is acquired (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.fee: $10 per dog (lifetime license); no tax for a trained guide, hearing or service dog
steps.quote: To purchase a tag, the dog owner must present a valid rabies vaccination certificate for the dog along with a completed dog license application.

steps.step: The Treasurer checks the certificate and residence, then issues the license receipt and metal tag
steps.how: The Treasurer may license only dogs whose owners live within the city and may require information showing this from any applicant. With a proper application and a current vaccination certificate, the Treasurer records the owner's name and address, payment date, tag serial number and the dog's sex and spay or neuter status, and gives you a license receipt and a metal tag. These license records are open to public inspection while the license is valid.
steps.quote: Proof of a current, valid rabies vaccination must be supplied before a dog license can be issued (City Code §3.2-65).

steps.step: Put the tag on the dog's collar and keep the receipt
steps.how: Fasten the tag to a sturdy collar that the dog wears. Keep the license receipt and show it if an animal control officer or other officer asks. The collar and tag may come off while the dog is lawfully hunting, competing in a dog show, confined, under your immediate control, or has a skin condition a collar would worsen. A dog without a tag is presumed unlicensed, and untagged dogs found on city streets are taken to a shelter.
steps.quote: Dog license tags shall be securely fastened to a substantial collar by the owner or custodian and worn by such dog.

steps.step: If you have not applied, expect a license application from the Treasurer
steps.how: The Treasurer matches the rabies certificates veterinarians send in against licensed dogs. If no license was bought within 90 days of the vaccination, the office mails the owner an application with instructions. Complete it and pay as in s4 and s5. This mailing does not extend the legal deadline: the license tax is still due within 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old or is acquired (s5; Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A)).
steps.deadline: 90 days after the date of vaccination (Va. Code § 3.2-6529(B))
steps.quote: If a dog license is not purchased within 90 days, our office will automatically send you a dog license application with instructions on how to purchase a license.

steps.how: The lifetime license stays valid only while you live in the City of Charlottesville and the dog's rabies vaccination is kept current. Keep the dog's rabies shots up to date. If you move out of the city, license the dog with the treasurer where you now live. If the rabies certificate has expired, the City's FAQ says to vaccinate the dog and then contact the Treasurer's Office.
steps.quote: The lifetime license shall be valid only as long as the animal’s owner resides in the City of Charlottesville and the dog’s rabies vaccination is kept current.

steps.step: Replace a lost, destroyed or stolen tag
steps.who: Owner or custodian; City Treasurer's Office
steps.how: Apply to the Treasurer's Office for a duplicate tag and show the original license receipt. State law has the owner make an affidavit (a sworn statement) before the Treasurer that the tag was lost, destroyed or stolen. The Treasurer notes the duplicate's number and date on the original receipt. Put the new tag on the collar right away.
steps.deadline: At once, as the statute states (Va. Code § 3.2-6532)
steps.quote: If a dog or cat license tag is lost, destroyed or stolen, the owner or custodian shall at once apply to the treasurer or his agent who issued the original license for a duplicate license tag, presenting the original license receipt.

steps.step: Kennels only: buy an annual kennel license
steps.who: Kennel operator (an establishment keeping five or more dogs for breeding, hunting, training, renting, buying, boarding, selling or showing); City Treasurer's Office
steps.how: The City Code sets an annual kennel license for a kennel of 20 dogs or of 50 dogs, payable at the Treasurer's Office. The Dog Tags page and the application do not mention kennels, so ask the Treasurer's Office how to apply.
steps.deadline: Due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(C)); the kennel license runs January 1 to December 31 (City Code § 4-37(b))
steps.fee: $20.00 annually for a kennel of 20 dogs; $35.00 annually for a kennel of 50 dogs
steps.quote: The license for a kennel shall run from January 1 to December 31, inclusive.

escalation.trigger: The Treasurer will not issue the license because the dog's rabies vaccination has expired or no certificate is shown
escalation.next: A licensed veterinarian (vaccinate the dog), then the City Treasurer's Office again
escalation.basis: https://www.charlottesville.gov/Faq.aspx?TID=44 (City Treasurer - Dog Tags FAQ); Va. Code § 3.2-6526(B)
escalation.quote: Please vaccinate your dog as soon as possible and then contact the Treasurer’s Office for assistance.

escalation.trigger: The dog cannot safely be vaccinated because of a documented medical condition
escalation.next: The local health director (Virginia Department of Health), on an exemption request from the dog's veterinarian; then present the exemption certificate to the City Treasurer
escalation.deadline: An approved exemption is valid for one year and must then be renewed, or the dog vaccinated
escalation.quote: The local health director, in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, may grant an exemption to the requirement for rabies vaccination

escalation.trigger: The license tax is charged for a trained guide, hearing or service dog
escalation.next: City Treasurer's Office: ask that the state exemption be applied
escalation.quote: No license tax shall be levied on any dog that is trained and serves as (i) a guide dog for a blind person, (ii) a hearing dog for a person who is deaf or hard of hearing, or (iii) a service dog for a mobility-impaired or otherwise disabled person.

escalation.trigger: The City Treasurer declines because the owner does not live within the city limits
escalation.next: The treasurer (or other licensing officer) of the county or city where the owner lives, for example Albemarle County for county residents with a Charlottesville mailing address
escalation.quote: shall only have authority to license dogs and cats of resident owners or custodians who reside within the boundary limits of his county or city and may require information to this effect from any applicant

escalation.trigger: The dog is picked up by Animal Control without a tag
escalation.next: The public animal shelter the City uses: reclaim the dog, have it vaccinated and buy the license. The owner may be charged the actual cost of keeping the dog impounded (§ 3.2-6546(C)).
escalation.deadline: The shelter must hold the dog for not less than five days, counted from the day after it is confined, unless the owner claims it sooner; five more days if the dog has a collar, tag, license, tattoo or other identification (§ 3.2-6546(C)). An unclaimed dog is then deemed abandoned and becomes the shelter's property (§ 3.2-6546(D)).
escalation.quote: An animal confined pursuant to this section shall be kept for a period of not less than five days, such stray hold period to commence on the day immediately following the day the animal is initially confined in the facility, unless sooner claimed by the rightful owner thereof.

escalation.trigger: A summons for keeping an unlicensed dog or for not paying the license tax
escalation.next: Charlottesville General District Court (appear on the date on the summons; bring the license receipt if the dog is licensed)
escalation.deadline: The court date on the summons
escalation.quote: in any proceedings under this chapter the burden of proof of the fact that such dog or cat has been licensed, or is otherwise not required to bear a tag at the time, shall be on the owner of the dog or cat

escalation.trigger: Convicted in the General District Court
escalation.deadline: Within ten days from the conviction
escalation.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

caveats: City code citation resolved. The Dog Tags page and the application cite 'City of Charlottesville Code Section 3.2-65' or 'City Code §3.2-65', the FAQ calls it 'State Code Section 3.2-65', and the 2017 flyer 'state code section 3.2-65'. No such City Code section exists. The number matches Virginia Code Title 3.2, Chapter 65 (Comprehensive Animal Care). The City's own dog license sections are City Code §§ 4-36 and 4-37 (Chapter 4, Animals and Fowl, Article III, Dogs Generally).

Local ordinance source. The City Code text is quoted from the proposed ordinance in the November 20, 2017 City Council agenda packet on the City's CivicClerk agenda system (fileId 1137, the dog license item, which reprints the November 6, 2017 staff report). That page is marked up. Only unchanged or underlined (added) text is quoted; struck text is left out. The November 20, 2017 minutes (fileId 1136) list it as consent agenda item j, 'ORDINANCE: Proposed Changes to Dog License (2nd reading)', and record that 'The consent agenda passed.' The staff report says the change took effect with the tag year starting January 1, 2018. The current codified text on Municode (https://library.municode.com/va/charlottesville/codes/code_of_ordinances) has not been checked: Municode's terms of use are not confirmed to allow it. CivicClerk searches for 'dog license', 'Section 4-37', 'kennel', 'Animals and Fowl' and 'license tax' dog (to 2026-10-11) found only the 2017 dog license item (and unrelated zoning and report items), so no later amendment is known, but the current codified text has not been compared. Subsection numbering: in the adopted ordinance, item (a)(2) (the unneutered-dog rate) is struck in full but the kennel items keep their labels (3) and (4). The kennel citations here follow that text; the codified Code may have renumbered them (for example to (a)(2) and (a)(3)).

City Code § 4-37(c), as adopted in 2017, exempts service dogs only for a 'mobility-impaired person'. Va. Code § 3.2-6528(A) as it now reads also exempts a service dog for an 'otherwise disabled person', with definitions taken from Va. Code § 51.5-40.1. The state exemption applies by its own terms. Emotional support, comfort or companionship animals are not service dogs under § 51.5-40.1.

The Dog Tags page still speaks of a 'renewal form' and of a vaccination that 'expires before the new license year begins'. That wording is left over from the annual licenses used before 2018. The application says the City has issued only lifetime tags since 2018. Neither the City pages nor the 2017 ordinance say whether a lifetime license must be bought again after the dog's rabies vaccination lapses. The FAQ says only that with an expired certificate 'you will not have the option to purchase a renewal license' and to vaccinate, then contact the Treasurer's Office.

The 2017 flyer is outdated in two places. It says the Treasurer sends an application if no license is bought within 60 days of vaccination; the current FAQ says 90 days, which matches Va. Code § 3.2-6529(B). It also lists the SPCA as a place to buy tags; the current Dog Tags page names only mail and the City Hall lobby. Va. Code § 3.2-6527 lets the Treasurer appoint agents and substations, but no current agent was found. Check with the Treasurer's Office before going anywhere else.

Payment details. The Payment Methods page says the City Hall counter takes cash, checks, debit cards and money orders, and that mailed payments must be checks or money orders. Its phone and online payment lists (parking tickets, property taxes, utility bills) do not include dog licenses, so no online purchase was found. Credit cards are refused at the counter 'for tax payments'. The page does not say whether the dog license tax counts as a tax payment for that rule. No payee name for checks is stated for dog licenses. The page also lists drop boxes at City Hall for check and money order payments, but no City page says a dog license application may be left there, so the drop boxes are not listed as a route in s5.

Residence. The City Treasurer can license only dogs of owners who live inside the city (Va. Code § 3.2-6527). Many Albemarle County residents have Charlottesville mailing addresses, and they license through the county. Albemarle's process is not covered on this page.

Newcomers. State law ties a license to the owner's locality: the treasurer licenses residents only, and a lifetime license is valid only while the owner lives in the issuing locality (§ 3.2-6530(B)). But neither state law nor the City pages give an explicit deadline for a person who moves into the city with a dog licensed elsewhere. The 30-day rule in § 3.2-6530(A) is written for dogs reaching 4 months or being acquired.

Penalties. City Code § 4-36 makes owning or keeping an unlicensed dog 4 months or older a Class 4 misdemeanor. Va. Code § 3.2-6587(A)(2) makes it a Class 4 misdemeanor to fail to pay the tax 'before February 1 for the year in which it is due', and lets the court order the dog confiscated. A Class 4 misdemeanor carries a fine of not more than $250 (§ 18.2-11(d)), and paying after a summons does not avoid court costs (§ 3.2-6536). How the February 1 date applies to a one-time lifetime license is not explained by any source read.

No administrative appeal of a Treasurer licensing decision was found, either in state law or on the City pages. The Treasurer is an elected constitutional officer. Refund provisions for erroneously assessed local taxes (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3980, 58.1-3984, 58.1-3990) are written for taxes assessed by a commissioner of the revenue under Title 58.1. Whether they reach the Title 3.2 dog license tax, which is paid on application, was not established, so they are not listed as an escalation route.

Shelter. The Dog Tags page says untagged dogs 'are taken by Animal Control to a shelter where they remain until the owner pays for the vaccination and obtains the proper tag', but it does not name the shelter. The 2017 staff report says the CASPCA was consulted. Which shelter the City now uses, and its reclaim fees and hours, are not confirmed.
Cats. No Charlottesville cat license was found: the 2017 ordinance and the City pages cover dogs only. Cat licensing is optional for localities under Va. Code § 3.2-6524(B).

Rabies vaccination cost is set by veterinarians or clinics and is not stated by any City source. Va. Code § 3.2-6521(B) requires the city to make sure a rabies clinic is held at least once every two years. No current Charlottesville clinic schedule was found.

Office email. The Treasurer page's contact box gives citytreas@charlottesville.gov, which is recorded here. The page body, the application and the 2017 flyer give citytreas@charlottesville.org. Both are the office mailbox.

Privacy. The Treasurer page, the application, the 2017 packet and the minutes name the elected Treasurer, staff and council members, and the Animal Control page names an officer. None of these names is recorded here; only office channels are.
The Dog Tags page's sentence 'Dog tags may be purchased by mail, in the lobby of City Hall.' is read here as two options: by mail, or in person in the City Hall lobby.

State law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, not to the law.lis.virginia.gov pages linked in each citation. Regulation quotes come from the Virginia Administrative Code page on law.lis.virginia.gov.

The 36 state-law quotes (26 legal_basis, 3 steps, 2 fees, 5 escalation) are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section with whitespace normalised only, and each subsection label matches the text. The 27 other quotes were matched against sources re-fetched on 2026-10-11: the Dog Tags page (/553/), the Dog Tags FAQ (served at /m/faq?cat=44), the Dog License Application PDF (/DocumentCenter/View/3873, extracted as UTF-8 so the curly apostrophes match), the 2017 Council packet (CivicClerk fileId 1137) and 12VAC5-105-30 on law.lis.virginia.gov.

City Code quotes: the packet page with §§ 4-36 and 4-37 (page 75 of fileId 1137) was rendered and checked by eye. Every quoted City Code clause is unchanged or underlined (added) text; none is struck. The minutes (fileId 1136) confirm consent agenda item j, 'ORDINANCE: Proposed Changes to Dog License (2nd reading)', and 'The consent agenda passed.' (adopted without item i only).

Summary: said a current certificate 'or a vet's medical exemption'. Under 12VAC5-105-30 the exemption is granted by the local health director on the veterinarian's application; the summary now says so.
